data.name: Project Remedium
data.detailed_description:
In this first game by Atomic Jelly, a nanobot journeys through a human organism to revert the effects of strange illness and a set of unfortunate events that occurred.

Armed with once purely medical equipment that now became a duo of adaptive weapons - the Energy Cannon and the Remedium Sprayer - and able to travel in a fast and agile way with help of an invaluable grapnel, Nano+ can fight pathogens, mutated organisms and deranged nanobots, heal, help his allies and interact with a unique environment.

Nano+ is not alone in hist struggles: the veteran nanobot SuperVisette will guide him through the journey and the last sane nanobots struggling to maintain health and order will also help however they can.

Features:

  • upgradeable weapons for damage dealing and accelerated healing
  • versatile grapnel for climbing and quick getaways
  • substance crafting for improving both treatment methods and feats of Nano+
  • interactive environment with infected tissue and ailments
  • a story to discover and friendly nanobots to provide aid
  • various missions related with healing and helping fellow bots
  • bloodstream and 6 organs to heal

Genre: story-driven Action Shooter

Platform: PC

data.short_description: Project Remedium is a story-driven action shooter set inside a human body devastated by illness and bad circumstances. It's a post-apocalypse of sorts, a really tiny one, but for a nanobot named Nano+, the body is a whole world. So he is hell-bent on fixing it with his guns and a unique grapnel.

reviews.review:
Project Remedium is an imaginative first-person action game developed by Atomic Jelly and published by Atomic Jelly in collaboration with Movie Games S.A. Instead of placing players in a war-torn city or a futuristic battlefield, it shrinks the conflict to a microscopic scale inside the human body. Players assume the role of Nano+, a medical nanobot designed to combat infection and repair biological damage from within. This unusual premise immediately gives the game a distinct personality, transforming organs, blood vessels, and infected tissue into expansive environments filled with danger, exploration, and scientific creativity. While many independent shooters rely on familiar science fiction settings, Project Remedium succeeds in standing apart through its original concept alone.

The campaign follows Nano+ as it attempts to restore a critically ill body by eliminating viruses, mutated organisms, and malfunctioning machines that threaten its survival. Along the way, players encounter fellow nanobots, receive guidance from experienced allies, and gradually uncover the circumstances that led to the internal crisis. The narrative is relatively simple, but it provides enough motivation to keep the journey engaging without interrupting the pace of the action. The microscopic perspective also allows ordinary biological processes to become fascinating landscapes, making every new location feel fresh while reinforcing the game's unique medical theme.

Combat revolves around specialized equipment that functions as both weapons and medical tools. Nano+ uses devices such as the Energy Cannon and the Remedium Sprayer to destroy hostile organisms while simultaneously restoring damaged areas and supporting friendly units. This combination of offensive and restorative mechanics creates a satisfying gameplay loop that goes beyond traditional run-and-gun shooting. Battles encourage constant movement thanks to a grappling device that allows players to quickly reposition, traverse vertical environments, and escape overwhelming enemy attacks. The mobility system adds speed and flexibility to encounters, preventing combat from becoming static while rewarding players who make full use of the environment.

Character progression further expands the experience through weapon upgrades and crafting systems that allow Nano+ to improve both combat effectiveness and medical capabilities. Gathering resources during exploration provides meaningful incentives to search beyond the main objectives, while upgrades gradually unlock stronger treatment methods and more efficient equipment. The game also introduces a variety of infected creatures and mechanical threats that require players to adapt their tactics, even if some enemy encounters eventually begin to repeat themselves during the later stages of the adventure. Although the progression systems are not overly complex, they provide enough customization to keep the gameplay rewarding throughout the campaign.

One of Project Remedium's greatest achievements is its environmental design. The developers successfully transform the interior of the human body into an imaginative science fiction world where organs become explorable regions and biological structures serve as believable battlegrounds. Each location features its own visual identity while maintaining the overall medical theme, helping the world feel cohesive despite its fantastical presentation. The artistic direction effectively compensates for technical limitations, as the game prioritizes originality over photorealistic visuals. Interactive environments and healing-focused objectives also reinforce the idea that players are not simply defeating enemies but actively restoring life from within.

Despite its originality, the game does have noticeable shortcomings. Enemy AI lacks sophistication in certain encounters, and mission objectives can occasionally feel repetitive after the initial novelty begins to wear off. Some animations, visual effects, and overall production values reveal the limitations of its independent budget, and the story could have benefited from deeper character development and stronger world-building. Nevertheless, these flaws rarely overshadow the creativity behind the game's central concept. The unique setting, enjoyable traversal mechanics, and satisfying blend of shooting, exploration, and healing make it an experience that feels refreshingly different from most shooters in its category.

Project Remedium may not deliver the level of refinement found in blockbuster action games, but it offers enough originality and engaging mechanics to leave a lasting impression. Its inventive premise, fast-paced combat, meaningful progression systems, and distinctive biological environments combine to create a memorable adventure that embraces creativity over convention. Players looking for a fresh take on the first-person shooter genre will likely appreciate the game's willingness to experiment, even if some aspects fall short of their full potential.

Rating: 4/10
